punchline: Thich Nhat Hanh says anger is like a raw potato: you cannot eat it until it has cooked.
thirty_sec: Thich Nhat Hanh compares anger to a potato. A raw one can't be eaten, so it goes on the fire, and the fire is mindfulness. When anger rises, you start breathing mindfully right away and hold the anger while you breathe. You try not to say or do anything yet. He has another picture too: garbage turns into compost, and compost into a flower. Looked after, anger changes into something else.
